laws.rule: Drivers may not use a hand-held phone or other wireless device to read, type or send a text, instant message, email or web page while driving (Nebraska Revised Statutes 60-6,179.01). Hands-free and voice-operated use is allowed. It is a secondary offence: police enforce it only when a driver is also stopped or charged for something else.

A motorised boat registered in another state needs a Nebraska Aquatic Invasive Species (AIS) stamp for each calendar year it is used in Nebraska, including when launched from a Nebraska ramp on a border river. The stamp goes on the right-hand rear side of the boat, above the waterline. It is sold online through Game and Parks and by permit vendors.

items.text: Adult-use (recreational) cannabis is not legal in Nebraska. Possessing 1 ounce (about 28 g) or less of marijuana is an infraction for a first offence: a citation, a US$300 fine (about A$426 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040) and possibly a drug education course. A second offence is a misdemeanour with a US$400 fine and up to 5 days in jail (Nebraska Revised Statutes 28-416).

Voters passed the Nebraska Medical Cannabis Patient Protection Act in November 2024. It lets a patient with a written recommendation from a health care practitioner possess up to 5 ounces (about 140 g) of cannabis. The Nebraska Medical Cannabis Commission's rules require patients buying from Nebraska dispensaries to hold a recommendation from a practitioner listed in the state's directory, and were open for further comment in October 2026.

News reports say the Governor signed the Commission's regulations around 1 July 2026, after the Attorney General's review. As reported, they allow no more than 12 dispensaries statewide, cap purchases at 5 ounces in 30 days, and keep smoking, vaping and edible products banned.
The Nebraska Supreme Court unanimously upheld the two voter-approved medical cannabis laws in September 2026, after a challenge to the 2024 petition.
